result.result:
The app is built, and everything the spec asks for works end to end. But I couldn't compare any screen to Figma: its API was rate-limited for the whole run (HTTP 429, "retry after 398073 seconds", about 4.6 days), through both the MCP server and a direct REST call. So the layout and styling come from the written spec and the dsb component defaults. The "matches Figma in structure, spacing and proportion" acceptance point is unverified.

## What was checked
I scripted a headless-browser run against `npx @angular/cli@19 serve`. It checked:
- **Login:** submitting empty fields shows a red error state and a message on each field. `admin` / `admin` sets `isLoggedIn: true` and goes to `/dashboard`.
- **Guards:** a logged-out visit to `/users` goes to `/login`.
- **Dashboard:** a new log line appears every 3 seconds.
- **Profile menu:** it opens leftward and stays inside the viewport at both 1440px and 390px wide. It closes on an outside click, and Sign Out logs you out.
- **Dialogs:** all four open and close. Edit (`PUT`), invite (`POST`), and edit → Delete user → confirm (`DELETE`) all went through the in-memory API, and the table updated each time. The delete dialog closes on a backdrop click.
- **Console:** no errors. The production build is clean.

## Built from guesses (need a pass once Figma is back)
- **Dashboard grid:** four metric tiles, then a row of chart (two columns wide), service health and data summary, then logs full width.
- **Badge colours:** Admin dark, Editor blue, Viewer grey; Active green, Inactive grey.
- **Brand and footer:** the brand name "Blueprint", and the footer's link columns and legal links.
- **Date format:** the Joined column shows `Jan 15, 2024`.

## Token resolver: what it answered and what I did
- **Chart bars ("pure black"): no match.** I asked again in the design system's own terms ("filled high-contrast emphasis surface"). It resolved to `color-surface-emphasis`, the darkest fill the public tokens define, and that's what the bars use. The only pure black is the primary button's pressed state, and I didn't borrow it. There's a comment at `dashboard.component.css:95`.
- **Monospace font, and the app's base font: no match.** No font-family token exists, so these are the only literal values in the app. Each has a comment.
- **Log panel height and login card width: no match.** The log panel is eight lines tall. The login card uses the "small dialog" width token.
- **Where I overrode it:**
  - For "text on a dark surface" it returned a background token; I used `text-inverse`.
  - For "menu shadow" it returned a colour; I used `shadow-dropdown`.
  - For "page heading size" it returned the brand-name size (15px); I used the largest display size.

No palette tokens, private component tokens or colour literals are used anywhere. The only raw pixel values are four media-query breakpoints, because there are no breakpoint tokens and CSS can't use variables inside media queries.

## Gaps in the component library
- **Header:** `dsb-header` has no slot for an account control, so the profile menu is laid over the header's right edge, lined up with its inner width.
- **Header and footer links:** these are plain links, which reload the whole page and would wipe the in-memory data. The layout sends app-internal clicks through the router instead.
- **Dropdown clipping:** inside `dsb-modal`, the dropdown's option list was cut off because the modal body scrolls. I fixed it with a small override of the modal's internal styling, applied only to the edit and invite dialogs (`users.component.css:124`). It's worth reporting as a library bug.
- **Avatar fallback:** `dsb-avatar` doesn't fall back to initials when an image fails to load, so the users page catches the error itself and swaps in initials.

I replaced the original `package.json` with a fresh Angular 19 one and reinstalled; the dsb packages were already pulling in Angular 21. I also added `angular-in-memory-web-api@0.19.0`. I didn't look at the other arms' folders. The test scripts are in `/tmp/d1-e2e`, outside the project.
